output.title: Late payment terms: decide on one bounded check
output.body:
If you want to measure late payment terms, keep the decision narrow: are you still tracking due dates, agreed terms, and actual payment dates by memory or spreadsheet, or do you have a repeatable check that flags overdue invoices before they turn into a cash-flow surprise?

That is the part worth automating first. Not the whole finance process, just one recurring task: compare invoice date, agreed terms, and payment date; flag anything past due; and keep a simple log of what was late. If a collection action follows, a human approves it. Money movement stays human.

This is a pilot design, not a claim about a deployed system. The point is to see whether the workflow is frequent and repeatable enough to justify the work. If you are still reviewing invoices manually, the real question is how often that review happens and whether it is consistent enough to matter.

A practical next step is to audit one week of invoices. Note which were paid on time, which were late, and how long the manual review took. That gives you a bounded picture of the problem before you decide whether to build anything at all. No clipboard required.
